test_policy.notes: ACT/SAT are optional for international applicants and are not required for admission; if available they may be considered for undergraduate scholarship eligibility.

requirements.notes: International application has no fee. Needs passport copy, official transcripts (certified, with translations; undergraduate minimum cumulative GPA 2.0 after conversion to the US scale; 5 GCSE/IGCSE/O Level subjects at D or better), and an English score. After acceptance: Statement of Support and a bank statement showing at least $36,858 (the 2025-26 undergraduate estimate on the checklist) before the I-20 is issued. No essay required per the international admissions page.

deadlines.label: International fall 2027 application deadline (applying from abroad)
deadlines.notes: The dates are printed without a year, so fall 2027 is assumed. Applications incomplete by the deadline roll to the next session. Spring (January) entry: application Nov. 1, documents Nov. 15. Students transferring from a US school have later dates (fall: July 15).

deadlines.label: International fall 2027 document deadline
deadlines.notes: All admission documents must be received by this date (year not printed, so 2027 is assumed).

english_policy.waiver_notes: Exempt: citizens of listed English-speaking countries/territories; ACT composite 21 or SAT 1060; a US high school diploma (transcript reviewed, extra scores may be required); a US or English-speaking-country degree; IGCSE/GCSE/O Level English first language grade B or better; IB English Language & Literature HL score of 5 or higher. Also accepted: iTEP 3.5, MET 46, GTEC 1100, Oxford ELLT 6, TOEIC 586, EIKEN Pre-1, SAKAE 11-12. No conditional-admission or ESL pathway program is described on the pages read.

english.notes: For tests taken on or after 2026-01-21; the page prints 3.5 without naming the scale (assumed the new 1-6 band scale).

cost.notes: Student Account Services estimate for international undergraduates (15 credit hours per semester): tuition $18,000 plus fees $5,250 (entered as one combined figure), on-campus living for 9 months $12,620 (South Complex double, Residential Unlimited food plan), health insurance about $1,650 plus orientation/student service fees $600 (entered as other), total $38,120. Personal expenses ($4,500) and one-time vaccine/TB costs are listed separately and not included. Textbooks and a laptop are provided to eligible students per the cost page, so no books figure. The admissions cost page shows a different 'international' direct-expense estimate of $39,622

aid.notes: Northwest International Achievement Scholarship (NIAS): automatic for new international freshmen with a 2.75+ high school GPA; covers the in-state/out-of-state tuition difference (about $9,000 in year one), renewable with a 3.00 Northwest GPA, stackable with academic merit awards. Admission-based academic merit scholarships (GPA plus ACT/SAT chart) are automatic, with exceptional ACT/SAT scores helping; IB diploma award $1,000. No need-based aid for international students.

sat.note: The international pages print no SAT code; look it up in the College Board code search. SAT/ACT are optional.

act.note: The international pages print no ACT code; look it up at act.org.

toefl.note: No TOEFL institution code is printed on the pages read; look it up in the ETS code search.
